 Christina Applegate reveals MS misdiagnosis in shocking health update: ‘I lost everything’ 
 By 
 Jolie Zenna 
 Published 
 Oct. 20, 2026, 8:14 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Christina Applegate shockingly revealed she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis five years after receiving the diagnosis .
 “[My doctor] came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’” Applegate recalled through tears on her “MeSsy” podcast Tuesday.
 “I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy.”

 The actress explained that despite learning about the misdiagnoses, she still suffers from debilitating symptoms.
 “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better,” Applegate continued. “I haven’t gotten better. If anything, I’ve gotten worse.”
 The “Married… with Children” alum heartbreakingly admitted that she’s “back at square one” and has no idea where her health issues stem from now.
 “That’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”
 12 
 The actress (pictured in January) said she still suffers from debilitating symptoms, despite not having MS. christinaapplegate/Instagram 
 12 
 “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better. I haven’t gotten better. If anything, I’ve gotten worse,” she admitted. christinaapplegate/Instagram 
 The 54-year-old got emotional when she talked about how her MS diagnosis completely uprooted her life for the past five years.
 “I’ve gone through a great depression because of it. But I lost everything. I lost my job. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life. I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office.”
 Applegate continued, “I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”
 The “Dead to Me” star also spoke candidly about how it felt to no longer be a part of the MS community she was once the “poster child” for.
 12 
 The Emmy winner (pictured in 2023) said she is now “back at square one” since she and her doctors no longer know where her health issues stem from. Getty Images for Critics Choice Association 
 12 
 “That’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021,” she said. Emma McIntyre 
 “It’s weird because I feel like I let everybody down. It’s this weird feeling because I became this — you and I, the poster children for MS.”
 One of the hardest parts for Applegate after learning of the diagnosis, is that she no longer has something to pinpoint all of her struggles on.
 “I had a reason. I had a f—king reason as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don’t have a reason and it’s very unnerving and it’s very confusing for me.” 
 She also said she’s still in a “state of shock” over the misdiagnosis, calling it a “mindf—k.”
 12 
 Applegate (pictured at the 2024 Emmys) said that she feels she “let everybody down” in the MS community because she was the “poster child.” WireImage 
 12 
 Additionally, she no longer has something to pinpoint all of her struggles on. WireImage 
 Applegate co-hosts the “MeSsy” podcast with actress Jamie-Lynn Sigler who suffers from MS. 
 The “Don’t Tell Mom the Babysitter’s Dead” star, who hadn’t appeared on the podcast since March, explained that she took a step back to fully “process” the misdiagnosis while also dealing with “some health stuff.”
 During her two-part return to the podcast, the duo also had associate professor with the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center department of neurology, Doctor Marwa Kaisey as a guest to explain how the misdiagnosis occurred.
 Shockingly, the professional said MS misdiagnoses are “fairly common” due to the fact that “we don’t have one single test for MS. It’s not like we have something like a pregnancy test that says, yes. You have it. No. You don’t. It’s a list of criteria.”
 12 
 “I had a f—king reason as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don’t have a reason and it’s very unnerving and it’s very confusing for me,” Applegate (pictured in April 2025) confessed. Getty Images 
 12 
 The “Dead to Me” star (pictured in 2022) also brought a doctor on the podcast who shared that MS misdiagnosis are common because there isn’t one test for it. Getty Images 
 “Almost one in five of these people who’d been told they had MS, some for decades, didn’t actually have it,” Kaisey continued. “And a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS.”
 Applegate — who has been candid about her health battle since 2021 — was discharged from the hospital last month after a stay that began back in March .
 While it remains unclear why she was admitted, her rep told Page Six at the time, “She’s had a long history of complicated medical conditions that she has been refreshingly open about.”
 In April, without divulging details, the actress addressed the situation with fans. “Thank you for the outpouring of love and well wishes,” she wrote.
 “Health issues are a constant for me, but I’m a strong chick and I’m getting stronger and better every day.”
 12 
 Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP 
 12 
 Applegate has said she 
 The hospitalization was the latest medical challenge the “Bad Moms” star has faced in recent years. 
 In August 2025, she shared with “MeSsy” podcast listeners that a kidney infection had left her “screaming” and in the hospital with “so much pain.” 
 Additionally, in a February interview with People, Applegate revealed she was generally confined to bed and still trying to take her 15-year-old daughter, Sadie LeNoble , to school, saying it’s her “favorite thing to do.”
 “I tell myself, ‘Just get her there safely and get home so you can get back into bed.’ And that’s what I do,” she shared with the outlet.
